submission.natural_language_explanation: A sink-parked head: on fluent English prose it attends to the first token and stays below the line (predict ordinary English sentences inactive or weak, under ~0.25 of max). It fires when it leaves the sink for hard attention to the current or previous token. This happens once a text has built up a run of fragmented, low-frequency tokenization: digit groups and separators (-, :, .) of phone numbers, clock times and decimals, subword pieces of non-English words (Swahili, Indonesian, Polish), or terse code. It is strongest on the second and later items of such a run, for example the dashes of a second phone number or later Swahili subwords in a sentence, and weak on the first number or first foreign word in a text.

rival_explanations: Narrower: the head fires only on separators and digit groups inside numbers (phone numbers, times, decimals), so foreign-language subword text with no numbers is predicted inactive.

Broader: the head fires on any token of non-English or non-prose text (any foreign language, code or markup) from the start, with no build-up, so the first number or first foreign word in a text is predicted as strong as later ones.

Positional: the head leaves the first-token sink depending mainly on how far into a long document the token is, so ordinary English prose deep in a long text is predicted as active as numbers or foreign subwords.
